original_title: Synthesis of a Stable Hydrophilic trans ‐Cyclooctene Amino Acid Unlocks Fast Bioorthogonal Click Chemistry for the Generation of Antibody‐Drug Conjugates by Genetic Code Expansion
title: A trans-cyclooctene that doesn't fall apart in water, so you can actually click it
blurb: TCO/tetrazine click is the fastest bioorthogonal reaction around, but TCOs normally isomerize to the useless cis form under physiological conditions. This one's a hydrophilic, stable TCO amino acid that genetic code expansion drops straight into a protein, and the payoff is fast site-specific ADC assembly without babysitting the TCO's shelf life.

original_title: Synthesis of diphenylphosphinodithioic acid (DPPDTA) and application in an extraction chromatography resin for radiochemical separations of arsenic and selenium
title: A new resin for prying apart arsenic and selenium isotopes
blurb: As and Se ride together in the production chemistry for medical and security radioisotopes and their chemistry is annoyingly similar, so separating them usually means harsh acid or fussy redox control. This paper makes diphenylphosphinodithioic acid and bakes it into an extraction resin, aimed at the selectivity gap earlier thiol/thioether resins left on the table for Se.

original_title: Protein-State Editing through Proximity-Induced Targeted Delactylation
title: Dragging HDACs over to strip one lactyl mark off one protein
blurb: DeLacTACs are bifunctional molecules that hijack endogenous HDACs and point them at a specific lactylated lysine instead of degrading the whole protein. Proof of concept is YAP Lys90, where pulling off the lactyl group dials down YAP-TEAD signaling. Neat if it generalizes past one oncoprotein and one lysine.

original_title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
title: Native chemical ligation finally works at the junctions that used to break it
blurb: A pyridine-based ligation auxiliary that gets NCL through sterically ugly junctions, including beta-branched residues and O-glycosylated or O-phosphorylated amino acids, and tolerates acidic pH where NCL usually struggles. They also iterated the auxiliary scaffold enough to pull out a general design rule, which is the part worth remembering past this one paper.

original_title: Maleimide availability in thiol-maleimide peptide conjugation on PEGylated liposomes: a reactive-site accounting framework illustrated using hepatic drug-delivery systems.
title: Counting how many maleimides on your liposome are actually free to react
blurb: A framework for tallying reactive maleimide sites on PEGylated liposomes before you do thiol-maleimide conjugation, run through a hepatic drug-delivery example. Bookkeeping dressed up as a paper, but useful bookkeeping if your conjugation yields have ever come up mysteriously short.

original_title: Okgyeamides A–C: Cyclic Pentapeptides with Distinct Tyr–Trp C–C and C–N Cross-Links from a Cave-Derived Streptomyces sp.
title: Cave bacteria make pentapeptides with a crosslink chemists don't usually see
blurb: Okgyeamides A-C are cyclic YPWIP pentapeptides out of a cave-dwelling Streptomyces, carrying unusual Tyr-Trp C-C and C-N crosslinks nailed down by NMR, Marfey's, DP4+ and ECD. Genome mining turned up a P450 locus that fits a ribosomal origin, and okgyeamide A does scavenge ABTS radicals, though that's a mild assay result, not a drug lead.

original_title: Functional Characterization of Cross-Link Formation in Atropopeptide P450 Synthases
title: Three new P450s caught installing biaryl crosslinks in RiPPs
blurb: Atropopeptide P450 synthases stitch the C-C, C-N and C-O crosslinks into this RiPP class, and here KutB, KutC and NteB get the first in vitro workup of the group. NteB is the interesting one: it makes both bridge-above and bridge-below atropisomers from the same enzyme, which docking models are brought in to explain.

original_title: Development of Radioiodinated Tetrahydropyrazolopyridine Inhibitors Targeting mIDH
title: Iodinating a mutant-IDH1 inhibitor without losing potency
blurb: Starting from the SK60/SK87 tetrahydropyrazolopyridine scaffold, swapping in iodine on the benzyl group gives SK140 and SK148, both hitting IDH1 R132C at nanomolar potency and beating the parent compounds. The iodine isn't just there for binding, it's the handle for eventually making these into radiotracers.
venue: Journal of Labelled Compounds and Radiopharmaceuticals

original_title: Coupling Enzyme Activity to Host Survival via Genetic Code Expansion: An In Vivo Evolution System for Biocatalysts
title: Make the bacteria's survival depend on your enzyme working
blurb: An in vivo selection system where a noncanonical-amino-acid-producing biocatalyst has to work or the cell dies: the ncAA it makes feeds an orthogonal tRNA synthetase that reads through an amber stop codon to build a working chloramphenicol resistance gene. Turns "does this enzyme work" into "did the colony grow," which is a much easier screen to run at scale.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: The immunological landscape of antibody-drug conjugates: from target to payload biology
title: ADCs aren't just guided poison, they're also doing immunology
blurb: A review walking through how antibody-drug conjugates touch the immune system beyond dumping payload into a cell: Fc effector biology, payloads that trigger immunogenic cell death, and knock-on effects on the tumor microenvironment. Useful framing if you've only been thinking about ADCs as targeted cytotoxin delivery.

original_title: Copper‐Mediated Radiofluorination of the Excitatory Amino Acid Transporter 2 (EAAT2)–Targeted PET Tracer [ 18 F]RP‐115: Alternate Synthetic Method
title: A faster way to radiolabel the EAAT2 tracer
blurb: Copper-mediated radiofluorination swapped in for the multistep route behind [18F]RP-115, a CNS-penetrant prodrug that only becomes the active EAAT2-binding carboxylate once esterases cut it open in the brain. Same tracer, a shorter synthesis, which matters when you're racing fluorine-18's half-life to image glutamate transport in AD or ALS.
venue: Journal of Labelled Compounds and Radiopharmaceuticals

original_title: Patent map reveals the hidden knowledge hubs driving antibody-drug conjugate innovation - Bioengineer.org
title: Who actually owns ADC innovation
blurb: A patent-landscape analysis claiming to pinpoint the institutions and inventors sitting at the center of antibody-drug conjugate IP. More useful to a licensing lawyer scouting deals than to anyone at the bench.

original_title: Self-Crosslinked Oxidized Xyloglucan Hydrogels Enhance Macrophage Metabolism for Diabetic Wound Healing via the cAMP-PKA Pathway.
title: A self-crosslinking hydrogel that nudges macrophages toward healing
blurb: Oxidized xyloglucan hydrogels that crosslink on their own and push macrophage metabolism through the cAMP-PKA pathway, aimed at diabetic wounds that otherwise stall out in inflammation. Mechanism claim, not much else to go on yet.

original_title: Integrative characterization of cell-surface proximity interactions using DTSSP crosslinking and high-dimensional profiling.
title: Mapping who's touching whom on the cell surface
blurb: DTSSP crosslinking combined with high-dimensional profiling to catalog cell-surface proximity interactions, essentially a parts list of what sits next to what on the membrane. Solid groundwork, light on specifics beyond the method.

original_title: AimedBio and Boehringer Ingelheim initiate Phase I study of antibody-drug conjugate BI 4060107 - Business Wire
title: Another Boehringer ADC heads into Phase I
blurb: AimedBio and Boehringer Ingelheim are putting their antibody-drug conjugate BI 4060107 into humans for the first time. Just a trial starting, no safety or efficacy data to judge yet.

original_title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of (99m)Tc-Labeled Thalidomide Analogs as Novel Tumor-Targeting Radiopharmaceuticals.
title: Thalidomide gets a technetium tag for tumor imaging
blurb: Tc-99m-labeled thalidomide analogs designed and tested as tumor-targeting radiopharmaceuticals. An odd scaffold to build a tracer around given its history, but the chemistry is the actual point.

original_title: Modulating radiochemical behaviour and biodistribution of 211 At-FAPI via host–guest complexation
title: Caging astatine-211's awkward side chain in a host molecule
blurb: At-211 FAPI ligands need a lipophilic aryl group to get labeled, and that same group is what tanks their solubility and scrambles biodistribution. This swaps the usual organotin labeling for host-guest complexation to fix the physicochemistry without losing the fibroblast targeting that makes FAPI useful for alpha therapy.

original_title: Targeted radioligand therapy in oncology: clinical development across targets and platforms
title: Radioligand therapy's expansion past PSMA and SSTR
blurb: A review of where radioligand therapy is headed now that Lu-177 dotatate and Lu-177 vipivotide tetraxetan proved the concept works in the clinic. No new data here, just a map of which targets and platforms are following them in.

original_title: Mechanism of remarkable peptide modifications by the multinuclear non-heme iron-dependent oxidative enzymes ChrH/DybH
title: How a non-heme iron enzyme builds a hydantoin ring mid-peptide
blurb: ChrH and DybH are multinuclear non-heme iron enzymes that rearrange a two-cysteine peptide motif into a macrocycle plus a hydantoin, one of the odder moves in a family that already does heterocyclization, methylene excision, and oxidative cleavage. This paper goes after the actual mechanism instead of just cataloging that it happens.

original_title: Cysteine Cathepsins Mapped Across Breast Tumors Reveal States That May Shape Antibody-Drug Conjugate Use - Bioengineer.org
title: Cathepsin states in breast tumors could decide which ADC works
blurb: Mapping cysteine cathepsin activity across breast tumors to find states that might predict which antibody-drug conjugates actually get cleaved and released where they're supposed to. The logic tracks: ADC linker chemistry only pays off if the tumor has the right protease on hand.

original_title: Multicatalytic cooperativity enables divergent photobiocatalytic C–C couplings for scaffold diversification
title: 180 enzyme-photocatalyst pairs, sorted by who actually cooperates
blurb: The screen itself is the engineering win: 180 enzyme-photocatalyst combinations tested to find which ones productively cooperate on C-C couplings. Evolved PLP enzymes then steer the same coupling toward branched or linear non-canonical amino acids with real stereocontrol, so you pick the product shape by picking the enzyme.

original_title: Development of Radioiodinated Tetrahydropyrazolopyridine Inhibitors Targeting mIDH.
title: Radioiodinated tracers aimed at mutant IDH
blurb: Tetrahydropyrazolopyridine inhibitors carrying a radioiodine label, built to go after mutant IDH, label included so you can track it rather than just block it.

original_title: Terbium-161 Shows Dose-Dependent Edge Over Lutetium-177 in Mouse Neuroendocrine Tumor Model - Bioengineer.org
title: Terbium-161 edges out Lutetium-177 in mouse neuroendocrine tumors
blurb: Head-to-head dosing in a mouse neuroendocrine tumor model, and Tb-161 pulls ahead of Lu-177 with a dose-dependent advantage, presumably the extra low-energy electrons doing more local damage per decay. Mouse data only, nobody's run the human comparison yet.

original_title: Multimodal Evaluation of [(225)Ac]Ac-PSMA-617 Therapy in mCRPC: PET Based Total Tumor Volume, PSA Kinetics, and Blood Biomarkers.
title: Tracking Ac-225-PSMA-617 three different ways at once
blurb: A multimodal readout on Ac-225-PSMA-617 in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, pairing PET-based total tumor volume with PSA kinetics and blood biomarkers. More ways to measure whether it's working, not yet which measurement actually predicts outcome.

original_title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewis x Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
title: Building the sulfated sialic acid panel MERS actually binds
blurb: A chemoenzymatic route assembles a full panel of 6-sulfo sialyl Lewis x glycans, enzymatically built with protected GlcNAc swapped into specific positions and stripped off afterward, to finally pin down which sialoside MERS-CoV's spike actually prefers for that first attachment step.

original_title: Establishing Oxime as a Bioresponsive Group on Naphthalene Diimide: Visual Bacterial Classification and NIR-II Photothermal Antibacterial
title: A naphthalene diimide that snitches on bacteria by changing color
blurb: Bacteria reduce an oxime group on this naphthalene diimide to an iminyl radical, which cleaves the N-O bond and releases a hydroxyl radical, cycling through four distinct redox states and four colors along the way. Same reaction gives you a visual bacterial readout and a NIR-II photothermal kill mechanism, which is the neat part.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Molecular-Geometry-Guided Photocatalytic Dearomative Cyclization to Bis-spirolactams from Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes
title: Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes dearomatize their way to bis-spirolactams
blurb: Most spirocyclic chemistry stops at one spiro center; this is a photocatalytic dearomative cyclization, geometry-picked on the bicyclobutane substrate, that pushes the ipso cyclization to deliver bis-spiro lactams instead. More 3D character for drug-like scaffolds, if that gap in bis-spiro methods was actually the bottleneck.

original_title: Radioligand Binding to IDH1 Enzymes Revealed as Method-Dependent in New Study - Bioengineer.org
title: IDH1 radioligand binding depends on how you measure it
blurb: Same IDH1 enzyme, different assay methods, different binding numbers. Awkward thing to find out after a bunch of radioligand work already leaned on one method's reading.

original_title: A General Approach for the Generation of alpha-Thioalkyl Radicals from Pinacol Boronic Ester Precursors
title: Alpha-thioalkyl radicals, now from boronic esters
blurb: Pinacol boronic esters transesterify in situ with MeOBcat or 3-methoxycatechol, then an oxygen-centered radical knocks the thioalkyl radical off the boron. It traps onto enones and sulfonyl radical traps intermolecularly or cyclizes intramolecularly, giving a stable, shelf-friendly route into a radical class usually generated more messily.

original_title: 177Lu-PSMA Therapy in Recurrent High-Grade Glioma: A Pilot Study With Dosimetric Insights.
title: 177Lu-PSMA therapy, tried on brain tumors instead of prostate
blurb: A pilot run of Lu-177-PSMA therapy in recurrent high-grade glioma, with dosimetry data attached. The logic borrows straight from the prostate playbook since PSMA shows up on glioma neovasculature too, but it's a pilot, so the numbers are small.

original_title: Position-Selective Modification of Cyclic Peptides by Histidine-Directed β-C(sp3)–H Arylation of Alanine
title: Alanine gets its own C–H arylation handle, guided by histidine
blurb: A nearby histidine directs β-C(sp3)–H arylation right onto alanine in cyclic peptides, hitting penta- to decapeptides in moderate-to-good yield with real positional selectivity, and it tolerates noncanonical β, γ, δ, and ε amino acids too. They back it up with actual bioconjugation, tagging a fluorophore, a second peptide, and oleanolic acid onto the arylated product.

original_title: Photoelectrocatalytic Diazidation of Olefins via Synergistic Dual Iron Species
title: Two iron catalysts split the job of turning olefins into diazides
blurb: 1,2-diazidation of alkenes using TMSN3 as the azide source, run photoelectrochemically with two different iron species dividing the labor: one tunes how fast azide radicals form, which keeps the reaction from overoxidizing and holds selectivity. Mild conditions and broad substrate tolerance claimed, but it stops at the diazide, someone still has to reduce that to the diamine everyone actually wants.

original_title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ ortho ‐Substituted Dibenz[ c , e ]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
title: An enzyme reaches atropisomers chemocatalysis couldn't
blurb: Tetra-ortho-substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines are jammed enough that no catalytic asymmetric method existed for them at all. An engineered imine reductase gets there instead, the first biocatalytic route to atroposelective, congested bridged biaryls that had simply been off limits.

original_title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
title: Measuring bond strength in solution without the usual thermodynamic gymnastics
blurb: Getting an X-H bond dissociation free energy in solution has usually meant radical equilibration against a reference compound or a multi-step thermodynamic cycle, each step stacking its own error onto the next. This swaps that for a direct 2D-IR spectroscopic readout instead. If it holds up past the solvents shown here, it's a much less painful way to get a number people currently fight for.

original_title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
title: Turning one HTS hit into a flow-synthesis assembly line
blurb: A benzodiazepine hit against CDK11B gets run through an automated solid-phase flow platform, broken into a modular 10-11 step sequence so analogues come off the line instead of being hand-built one at a time. Proof-of-concept on a single scaffold, but it's the unglamorous plumbing that actually speeds up SAR once a hit's in hand.

original_title: Near-infrared excited core-shell upconversion composites for living cells proteome labeling.
title: Upconverting nanoparticles get pointed at the whole proteome
blurb: Core-shell upconversion composites excited by near-infrared light, used to label proteomes in living cells. Light on detail beyond that, but NIR excitation means less phototoxicity than the UV or visible probes it's meant to replace.

original_title: Visible-light-mediated stereoselective construction of oxa-spiro bicyclohexanes via strain-release [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition
title: Strained rings pop open to build oxa-spiro cages with light
blurb: A visible-light-driven [2π + 2σ] cycloaddition that releases ring strain to stitch together oxa-spiro bicyclohexanes stereoselectively. Thin on specifics beyond the mechanism, but strain-release cycloadditions are usually worth a look for how fast they build out 3D complexity.

original_title: Sustainable Electron Donor‐Acceptor Complex‐Mediated Decarboxylative C─C Coupling of Cinnamic Acids
title: Stilbenes from cinnamic acids, no metal and no photosensitizer required
blurb: Visible light and an electron donor-acceptor complex alone drive decarboxylative coupling of cinnamic acids with aryl diazonium salts into stilbenes, no transition metal and no photosensitizer, just ethanol and K2CO3. Good-to-excellent yields with high E-selectivity, and cutting out two whole catalyst classes is the actual selling point.

original_title: AstraZeneca’s ADC candidate beats expectations – new phase III data at ESMO - www.lifesciencefocus.com
title: AstraZeneca's ADC posts a phase III win at ESMO
blurb: New phase III data has AstraZeneca's ADC beating expectations, per the company's own ESMO presentation. That's the company's own numbers at a conference podium, so wait for the published data before getting too excited.

original_title: Compliance Mismatch Drives Mechanochemical Reactivity in Diels-Alder Reactions
title: A compliance-matrix rulebook for pulling molecules into reacting
blurb: Mechanical force reshapes a reaction's energy landscape, but nobody had a clean way to tie force direction, molecular structure, and the resulting barrier change together. This works it out through the compliance matrix across a systematically built set of cyclopentadiene Diels-Alder reactions. Under the harmonic approximation, the force-induced barrier shift reduces to a difference in compliances along the two directions you're pulling, tidy math for something that used to be hand-wavy.

original_title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
title: A phase-separation switch that only clusters T-cell receptors inside a tumor
blurb: Condenstim masks a CD3/CD28-clustering condensate system until a tumor-microenvironment protease cuts the mask off, so the T-cell activation signal only switches on where that enzyme is present. A clever way to make extracellular phase separation location-specific instead of just dumping the trigger everywhere.

original_title: Operando Surface Dynamics Govern the pH-Universal Activity and Stability of Cobalt Phosphide for Hydrogen Evolution
title: Cobalt phosphide's HER activity depends on which surface actually shows up
blurb: A data-mining pass over 2,282 experimental points, plus surface Pourbaix diagrams, AIMD, and microkinetic modeling, finds the real catalytic surface of CoP shifts with overpotential: hydroxide-covered below 100 mV, something else above it. Explains the pH-universal stability mechanistically instead of just reporting that it exists.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Lewis Acid Catalyzed Cyclizative Rearrangement Strategy for One-Step 3-SF5- Furoquinoline and Furopyridine Synthesis
title: One step from SF5 building blocks to fused SF5-heterocycles
blurb: A Lewis acid-catalyzed cyclizative rearrangement converts SF5 synthons straight into 3-SF5 furoquinolines and furopyridines in a single, atom-economical step, no multi-step workaround needed. The SF5 group is the draw here for anyone in pharma or materials who's wanted a modular route into it.

original_title: Direct Photochemical Decarboxylation at Sulfur(IV) through an Unusual Inner-Sphere Redox Process
title: Sulfoxides turn out to do ligand-to-metal-style charge transfer too
blurb: Acylated sulfoxides caught running an inner-sphere redox step under visible light: S+–O bond homolysis spits out a radical that decarboxylates, the kind of excited-state activation usually reserved for transition metals. A new photoactive intermediate class for organosulfur(IV) chemistry rather than a brand new transformation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Trace-level quantification of N-Nitroso diclofenac in diclofenac sodium by LC–MS/MS using an in-source fragmentation based MRM strategy
title: Hunting the nitrosamine hiding inside diclofenac
blurb: An LC-MS/MS method using in-source fragmentation MRM transitions quantifies trace N-nitroso diclofenac in both the drug substance and the tablets. Unglamorous, but exactly the assay regulators have been demanding since the nitrosamine impurity scares started.

original_title: Synthesis of Thiophene-Fused π-Systems from Diarylethylenes via C–H Thienannulation and Mechanistic Studies
title: Thiophenes fused on with nothing but sulfur and heat
blurb: Diarylethylenes plus elemental sulfur close into thiophene-fused pi-systems with no catalyst and no additive, up to 98% yield, and it scales to grams. They pin the mechanism to a thiolate anion domino process. Cheap chemistry that actually holds up at scale is the rare part.

original_title: A General Cobalt-Catalyzed Oxidative Radical-Polar Crossover Platform for Secondary and Primary Alkyl Radicals
title: Oxidative radical-polar crossover finally works on the boring alkyl radicals
blurb: Photoredox ORPC has mostly only handled stabilized radicals, since secondary and primary alkyl radicals oxidize too reluctantly and die too fast to catch. A cobalt-catalyzed platform gets around that, opening carbocation-mediated alkylation of heteroatom nucleophiles to radicals photoredox couldn't touch before.

original_title: N-Heterocyclic Carbene/Organic Photoredox-Cocatalyzed Three-Component Tetralin Synthesis
title: Building tetralins from acyl fluorides and two styrenes in one pot
blurb: NHC and organic photoredox catalysis cooperate to stitch acyl fluorides and styrenes into fully substituted tetralins with complete regioselectivity, no metal involved. The path runs through a radical cation from one alkene reacting with a second alkene and a ketyl radical, three components assembled in a single operation.

original_title: Design, Synthesis, and Biological Evaluation of 99m Tc‐Labeled Thalidomide Analogs as Novel Tumor‐Targeting Radiopharmaceuticals
title: Thalidomide gets a Tc-99m tag and a shot at tumor imaging
blurb: Three thalidomide analogs (DPDQA, ADPB, CQHC) are directly radiolabeled with Tc-99m using sodium dithionite, with pH, ligand and reductant loading, and reaction time all optimized for labeling. Repurposing thalidomide's targeting behavior as the business end of an imaging agent, rather than its original job, is the actual hook.
venue: Journal of Labelled Compounds and Radiopharmaceuticals

original_title: High-Entropy Materials for Electrochemical Gas Conversion
title: A review asks what high-entropy materials actually buy gas electrocatalysis
blurb: High-entropy materials get their configurational-disorder pitch reviewed specifically for gas-involved electrocatalysis: entropy-driven design rules, entropy-guided synthesis, nanoscale structural control, and how people are even characterizing these messy multi-element surfaces. It's a review, so no new data, just the case for why the disorder is worth the trouble here.

original_title: Back-to-monomer depolymerization of silicones by deoxygenative chlorination
title: Silicones get an actual way back to monomer
blurb: Deoxygenative chlorination cleaves the Si-O backbone and turns spent silicone polymer back into its starting monomers, the depolymerization step silicone recycling has been missing. Nice trick if it holds up on real cured silicone and not just clean lab polymer.

original_title: Direct C–H Phosphorothiolation of Indoles under Visible-Light Irradiation
title: C3-phosphorothiolation of indoles, no photocatalyst, no stinking thiols
blurb: Visible light, cheap KI as catalyst, and air as the oxidant install a phosphorothiolate at indole's C3 without the usual malodorous thiol reagents or hazardous peroxides, using an odorless phosphorothioate instead. Transition-metal-free, and the products convert on to a range of dithio compounds.

original_title: Electroenzymatic Sequential Catalysis for Enantiodivergent Synthesis of Halohydrins
title: One enzyme system, either enantiomer of your halohydrin
blurb: Electrochemistry driving an enzyme does site-selective C-H hydroxylation on alkylarenes, and depending on which way you run it you get either enantiomer of the halohydrin, plus methyl mandelate and a beta-nitro alcohol, under mild conditions with good yields and ee. The same setup also deracemizes beta-chlorohydrins on the side.

original_title: Tracking the Ultrafast Dynamics of Carbon–Carbon Bond Formation Following CH 3 I Photodissociation on Amorphous Silicon Oxide Surfaces
title: Catching C-C bond formation in the act on a silicon oxide surface
blurb: Femtosecond pump-probe spectroscopy paired with time-of-flight mass spec tracks what happens in the moments after 266 nm light blows CH3I apart on amorphous silicon oxide, following the radicals as they couple into a C-C bond. Surface radical coupling is normally too fast to resolve, so the methods flex is the actual point here.

original_title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
title: Quaternary stereocenters from a photoredox/nickel tag team
blurb: Photoredox and a chiral nickel catalyst work in tandem to turn beta-keto esters and styrenes directly into enantioenriched 1,4-dicarbonyls carrying an all-carbon quaternary stereocenter, radical addition then oxidation in one pot. Quaternary stereocenters are usually a slog to build asymmetrically, so doing it off two simple feedstocks in a single operation is the selling point.

original_title: Metal‐Free Reduction of CO 2 to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
title: Reducing CO2 to methanol with no metal in sight
blurb: Boron-appended N-heterocyclic nitrenium catalysts hydroborate CO2 all the way down to methoxide-level product at room temperature and 1 bar, with low catalyst loading and no metal in the mix. Swap catecholborane for borane dimethylsulfide and the selectivity shifts, so the reductant is doing as much work as the catalyst.

original_title: Development, Validation, and Application of a Highly Sensitive RP-HPLC Method for the Determination and Release Profile Comparison of Levonorgestrel from Silicone-Based Contraceptive Implants
title: An HPLC method for how fast your LNG implant actually releases drug
blurb: A reverse-phase HPLC method built to measure levonorgestrel release from silicone-based contraceptive implants, sensitive enough to compare release profiles across different implant formulations. Not a new drug, just the assay that lets you tell whether two silicone implants are actually releasing LNG at the same rate.

original_title: Synthesis of zigzag-type carbocationic nanobelts
title: A carbocationic nanobelt, zigzag style
blurb: Starting from resorcin[4]arene, fjord-stitching olefin metathesis plus selective bromination and a heterolytic C-Br cleavage builds a fully conjugated belt[4]arene[4]tropylium salt, four benzotropylium units fused into a closed carbocationic ring. It's the shortest possible segment of a zigzag carbon nanotube, a tidy model system for the quantum materials crowd even before anyone puts it in a device.

original_title: Regio- and Stereoselective Dimerization of Arylalkynes Mediated by a Transient Zinc Radical
title: Zinc radicals turn vinyl radicals into dimers instead of the usual tricks
blurb: A transient zinc radical attacks an alkyne to generate a vinyl radical, but instead of the usual hydrogen atom transfer or cyclization chemistry, it dimerizes into a diene. Running the dizinc compound (DIPPNacnacZn)2 with 1-phenylpropyne under UV gives a dizincated hexadiene with high regio- and stereoselectivity, a new reaction mode for an intermediate that's supposed to be predictable.

original_title: Diarylthiazolo[3,2- a ]pyridin-5-ones: All-Visible-Light-Activated Turn-off Mode Fluorescent Photoswitches with Near-Quantitative Conversion Efficiency
title: Fluorescent photoswitches that turn fully off on visible light alone
blurb: Two diarylethenes built on a thiazolo[3,2-a]pyridin-5-one core switch their fluorescence off with near-quantitative photocyclization, running entirely on visible light in solution and in solid films, and holding up well over repeated switching cycles. Turn-off switches that don't need UV to drive them are the harder ones to pull off.

original_title: Decentralized Biosynthesis of the Spiro-DKP Alkaloid Chevalinulin A Enabled by Nonclustered P450 and Intermolecular [4 + 2] Cyclase
title: A fungal Diels-Alderase that never bothered forming a gene cluster
blurb: Chevalinulin A, a spiro-DKP alkaloid from a deep-sea cold-seep fungus, turns out to be built by two enzymes that aren't even clustered together like fungal biosynthetic genes usually are. CalO, a P450, installs the exocyclic olefin the molecule needs, and FadA then runs an actual intermolecular [4+2] cycloaddition on the DKP core, something biology was barely known to do at all.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Recent Advance in Radiation Decay Radioisotopes for Targeted Nuclear Medicine and Cancer Treatment
title: A decay review that starts at half-life and lands on oncology
blurb: Walks through decay types and half-life, swings through energy, industry, space science and materials testing, then settles into its real focus: targeted nuclear medicine and cancer treatment. More orientation map than new result.
venue: International Journal of Innovative Science and Research Technology (IJISRT)

original_title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
title: A germanium Michael addition that doubles as a photoinitiator recipe
blurb: New reaction, the Germa-Michael addition, used to build a water-soluble, visible-light Type I photoinitiator with full regioselectivity. The pitch is nontoxic and aqueous-compatible photoinitiators are rare because efficiency, visible-light cure depth, and water solubility usually fight each other, and this one's engineered to hit all three.

original_title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
title: Oxoboranes finally stable enough to put in a vial
blurb: Oxoboranes have been a wanted main-group species for ages. Reacting a diboracumulene with carbonyl compounds now gives stable crystalline ones with exceptionally short, strong B–O bonds, not just a fleeting intermediate someone trapped once.

original_title: Where a radioactive emitter sits inside a tumour cell changes simulated dose - Bioengineer.org
title: Where the isotope parks inside the cell changes its own dose math
blurb: A simulation showing that subcellular location of the emitter shifts the modeled dose it delivers to a tumor cell. Worth remembering next time a dosimetry model treats the whole cell as one uniform target.

original_title: Prognostic Value of 177Lutetium-PSMA Single Photon Emission Tomography and Timing of Response
title: A trial asking whether Lu-177-PSMA SPECT can predict who responds, and how fast
blurb: Completed study out of a Nancy hospital looking at whether Lu-177-PSMA SPECT imaging and the timing of the response carry prognostic value. It's a trial registry entry, not results in hand yet.

original_title: Modular Synthesis of Azulene-Derived Nonbenzenoid Arenes through Alternating Chemical Reactivity
title: Azulene's lopsided orbitals turned into a synthesis rulebook
blurb: Azulene's frontier orbitals flip character depending on position, and this turns that into an alternating reactivity model, core to substituent, for directing π-extension in a controlled way. Aimed at nonbenzenoid PAHs for optoelectronic and magnetic materials, where regioselective build-out has mostly been trial and error.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Constructing the Transfer Ladder between Active Sites and Functional Units within the Cluster-Based Catalyst for Reductive Amination
title: Making a catalyst hand ammonia from storage to the active site
blurb: The mesoporous phosphotungstate framework soaks up ammonia fine but can't catalyze reductive amination on its own, while the Pd3 cluster catalyzes but starves for ammonia nearby and loses activity and selectivity. Wiring the two together builds a relay that ferries ammonia from the reservoir to the cluster doing the actual chemistry.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Innovative and eco-friendly electro-organic synthesis of carbazole derivatives and evaluation of their antiviral and anticancer potential
title: Carbazoles from one electrochemical pot, antiviral screen included
blurb: Electro-organic coupling of bromobenzene and nitrobenzene on a custom Mg electrode in a deep eutectic ionic liquid, pitched as green, that builds carbazoles and checks them for antiviral and anticancer activity. The mechanism description piles together electrocyclization, Buchwald-Hartwig amination, and domino C-H activation in one breath, which is a lot of named chemistry to claim at once, so I'd want to see the actual data before buying the "remarkable efficiency."
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Science

original_title: Charge Loss of Proteins in vacuo: Implications for Native Mass Spectrometry and Ion Mobility
title: Native mass spec proteins are shedding charges mid-flight
blurb: Mass spectrometrists have swapped anecdotes about protein ions losing charge during native IM-MS for a while, and this is apparently the first real investigation of it. If charge state drifts inside the instrument itself, that's a problem given IM-MS structural interpretation depends on treating each charge state as its own distinct conformer.

original_title: Design principles and functionalization strategies of injectable hydrogels based on natural polymers for advanced wound healing.
title: Another hydrogel review for wound dressings, this time starting from natural polymers
blurb: A design-principles rundown on injectable hydrogels built from natural polymers and how to functionalize them for wound healing. It's a review, not a new material, so don't expect one standout result here.

original_title: Front Cover: Embedding a Dinuclear Ru─Pt Photocatalyst Into Polyampholytic Graft Copolymer Matrix Enables Prolonged Hydrogen Evolution While Allowing Catalyst Repair
title: A photocatalyst you can repair instead of replace
blurb: A dinuclear Ru-Pt photocatalyst embedded in a polyampholytic graft copolymer matrix keeps producing hydrogen longer than the catalyst alone manages, and the matrix lets you patch the catalyst up instead of binning it once it degrades. Cover art for Chemistry – A European Journal, but the repair angle is the actual hook.

original_title: Front Cover: Rhodium‐Catalyzed Synthesis of Enantioenriched α‐Substituted Primary Amines Through Asymmetric Transfer Hydrogenation
title: Rhodium hydrogenation makes chiral primary amines without the usual protecting-group detour
blurb: Asymmetric transfer hydrogenation with a rhodium catalyst gets you enantioenriched alpha-substituted primary amines directly. A front-cover piece, so take the fanfare with a grain of salt, but it's a clean route to a motif that's usually a pain to make enantiopure.

original_title: A study of excitation functions of deuterons induced reactions up to 50 MeV on <sup>160</sup>Gd using TALYS 2.0 & EMPIRE 3.2.3 for the production of <sup>160,161</sup>Tb
title: Modeling the deuteron route to medical Tb-160/161, no beam required
blurb: Pure TALYS 2.0 and EMPIRE 3.2.3 modeling of deuteron-induced reactions on Gd-160 up to 50 MeV, aimed at mapping the best production path for Tb-160 and Tb-161. All simulation, no actual irradiation, so it's homework for whoever runs the cyclotron next.

original_title: Thyra: bridging mass spectrometry imaging and SpatialData for unified multimodal analysis
title: A translator between mass spec imaging and the SpatialData format
blurb: Thyra plugs mass spectrometry imaging into the SpatialData ecosystem, so MSI data can sit alongside other spatial omics modalities in the same pipeline instead of living in its own silo.

original_title: Mass spectrometry-based affinity capture of peptide ligands from complex venom mixtures
title: Fishing receptor ligands straight out of raw venom
blurb: A membrane-based affinity capture workflow pulls GPCR- and ion-channel-binding peptides directly out of whole venom mixtures and hands them to mass spec for ID, skipping the low-throughput screening venom peptides usually demand. It recovers known ligands and flags new toxin candidates that still need validation.

original_title: Smart Gold Nanoprobe for CT Imaging of Granzyme-B Activity: towards Early Immunotherapy Response Monitoring
title: A gold nanoprobe that lights up on CT when immunotherapy is actually working
blurb: Gold nanospheres carrying a Granzyme B-cleavable peptide-PEG conjugate are built to report immune-cell killing activity via CT, aiming to catch whether immunotherapy is working before the usual follow-up scan would show it. Early-stage imaging work, but that's the whole point of it.

original_title: Sfh3 is a sterol-modulated PI/PI4P transfer protein that confers azole resistance in yeast by specifically mediating lanosterol/PI exchange
title: A yeast protein that swaps lanosterol for PI and ends up blocking azole drugs
blurb: Sfh3 is a sterol-modulated lipid transfer protein that specifically trades lanosterol for phosphatidylinositol rather than acting as a generic sterol shuttle, and ergosterol-pathway intermediates like lanosterol actually inhibit its ergosterol transfer. That lanosterol/PI exchange looks like the mechanism behind azole resistance in yeast, which matters to anyone still trying to get antifungals to work.

original_title: An Isolable Fused‐Metallacyclobutadiene Intermediate Enables Z ‐Selective Alkyne Dimerization via a Non‐Classical CCC ‐Pincer Platform
title: A pincer catalyst caught mid-reaction, and it only makes the Z-alkene
blurb: An osmapentalyne-based all-carbon CCC-pincer catalyst dimerizes terminal aryl alkynes head-to-head at a mild 50°C, and for once they isolated the fused-metallacyclobutadiene intermediate instead of just inferring it. Z-selective across a broad range of aryl and heteroaryl alkynes, notable since genuinely all-carbon pincer platforms are rare to begin with.

original_title: Electric-field control of hydrogen-bond ordering in monolayer ice on graphite
title: Flip a switch, flip the ice
blurb: Low-temperature STM shows an electric field alone driving monolayer ice on graphite from a mobile, non-wetting liquid-like adlayer into an ordered hexagonal solid, via field-driven charge redistribution at the interface. That's deterministic atomic-scale control over hydrogen-bond ordering, not just watching it happen.

original_title: Chromone Hydrazone-Based Fluorescent Chemosensor for Pb2+ Detection: Experimental and Theoretical Insights into a Turn-On Fluorescence Response
title: Only one of three chromone sensors actually lights up for lead
blurb: Three chromone hydrazone ligands made (FCMSH, CFCMSH, DCFCMSH), but only DCFCMSH flips from dark and quenched to a green glow when Pb2+ shows up, backed by theory as well as spectra. A 1-for-3 hit rate on turn-on fluorescence, which tells you how finicky this kind of sensor design still is.

original_title: Synthesis of 2-Amidothiophenes via Fiesselmann-Type Annulation of Activated Ynamides
title: Ynamides get a Fiesselmann-style route into amidothiophenes
blurb: Base-promoted hydrothiolation of activated ynamides with ethyl thioglycolate, then cyclization, gives regioselective 2-amidothiophenes. Mild, scalable, air-tolerant, and it holds up across a broad range of ynamides and electron-withdrawing groups, so this reads like an actual platform rather than a one-substrate trick.

original_title: Compact and Robust Scaffold for Visible-Light-Actuated Photoswitching
title: A photoswitch that flips with visible light instead of UV
blurb: A new push-pull photoswitch built on aryl azothiadiazole, small, stable in its Z form, and switching cleanly at 400/550 nm rather than demanding UV. Photoconversion efficiency depends on concentration, so there's no single universal irradiation recipe, just an optimized one for their conditions.

original_title: Transient matrix remodeling during direct cell-fate reprogramming enables self-assembly of dense neuronal niches
title: Turning fibroblasts into neurons tears up their own matrix on the way there
blurb: Reprogramming human dermal fibroblasts into neurons inside collagen microgels, the cells remodel the surrounding matrix mid-conversion, which lets dense neuronal niches self-assemble instead of settling for either tight cell packing or a defined ECM but never both. Using the identity switch itself as the construction tool is the neat part.

original_title: Deep-Learning-Decoded Spatial Electrochemiluminescence from Potentiostat-Free, Button-Battery-Driven Microneedle Arrays for Multiplexed microRNA Imaging
title: A button-battery microneedle patch reading out brain bleeds
blurb: No potentiostat needed: a gold-film copper microneedle array runs electrochemiluminescence straight off a button battery, with deep learning decoding the spatial signal for multiplexed microRNA detection tied to intracerebral hemorrhage. The whole point is swapping the usual bulky ECL rig for something that fits at the bedside.

original_title: Synthesis, Preclinical Evaluation, and Clinical Application of the FAPI-Dimer Based on the LARM Platform.
title: A FAPI dimer that made it all the way to the clinic
blurb: A dimeric FAPI tracer built on the LARM platform, carried from synthesis through preclinical testing into actual clinical use. No numbers to go on here beyond that it made the jump, which for a fibroblast-activation-protein tracer is the notable part.

original_title: pH-Responsive Dopamine-Grafted Polysaccharide Hydrogel with Enhanced Antibacterial and Hemostatic Properties.
title: A pH-sensing hydrogel that stops bleeding and fights bacteria at once
blurb: Dopamine grafted onto a polysaccharide backbone yields a pH-responsive hydrogel with boosted antibacterial and hemostatic performance, the classic wound-dressing pitch. Light on specifics here, but the dopamine graft is doing double duty as both adhesive and antimicrobial handle.

original_title: Ribozyme Redesign From an Existing RNA Scaffold Enables Multifunctional Hydrolysis for Molecular Release
title: One mutation turns a transfer ribozyme into a hydrolysis machine
blurb: Instead of evolving a new ribozyme from scratch, they repurpose an existing scaffold with a single-nucleotide mutation, flipping it from alkyl-transfer catalysis into a multifunctional hydrolysis ribozyme for molecular release. Deliberate redesign beating the usual slow selection process, at least for this one scaffold.

original_title: ADP-ribose induces neuronal ferroptosis through ENT2-mediated nucleotide rewiring
title: ADP-ribose is what's actually killing these neurons
blurb: NAD breakdown dumps ADP-ribose, which gets hauled in via the nucleoside transporter ENT2, rewires nucleotide pools, and triggers the ROS burst behind neuronal ferroptosis. Ties a metabolic byproduct directly to the cell death mechanism instead of just correlating with it.

original_title: Electrolyte Cation Engineering Selectively Regulates Competing Urea Oxidation Pathways
title: Swapping the electrolyte cation steers urea oxidation away from the bad pathway
blurb: Urea oxidation on Ni catalysts can slide into over-oxidized side products, and everyone's been trying to fix that by redesigning the catalyst surface itself. This shows the electrolyte cation, through noncovalent interactions alone, can selectively steer which pathway wins, a lever nobody had bothered pulling before.

original_title: Nucleophilic defluorination of PFAS under mild conditions
title: Taking PFAS apart one fluorine at a time, gently
blurb: A nucleophilic defluorination route that strips fluorine off PFAS under mild conditions instead of the usual brute-force heat or strong reductant. That's the whole appeal here, PFAS is notoriously stubborn to break down cleanly.

original_title: Dehalogenative Regiospecific Amination of 4-Bromo-1,1,2-trifluoro-1-butene with N -Heterocycles: Synthesis of 1,2-Difluorobuta-1,3-dien-1-yl Azaarenes
title: Skipping palladium and high-pressure acetylene to bolt difluorovinyl groups onto azaarenes
blurb: A dehalogenative amination that hooks N-difluorovinyl groups onto nitrogen heterocycles, straight off 4-bromo-1,1,2-trifluoro-1-butene. No transition-metal catalyst, no high-pressure acetylene, and it still lands excellent regio- and stereoselectivity with high yields across indole, benzimidazole, benzotriazole, and carbazole substrates.

original_title: Highly Selective Ionophore-Based Bilayer Emulsion Membranes
title: Swapping in ionophores where the biological channels usually go
blurb: Jammed interconnected bilayer emulsions, aqueous droplets stitched together by channel-studded bilayers, have been pitched as a stand-in for biological membranes, but the real channels' selectivity rarely survives the move into engineered versions. This one puts ionophores in the channels' place instead and builds a crosslinked version that's also mechanically tougher.

original_title: Best practices for handling MPTMS, preparing silanisation solutions, and washing the substrate after silanisation
title: Best practices for handling MPTMS, preparing silanisation solutions, and washing the substrate after silanisation
blurb: Hi everyone, I am currently working with mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane (MPTMS) in anhydrous toluene. I would appreciate some practical advice on how others handle silane reagents and perform silanisation in the lab for solution deposition, and how you wash after silanisation. How do you transfer silane using a pipette or syringe? I need suggestions from people who have worked with this silane.

title: Low yield in piperazine N-alkylation with 1-azido-3-chloropropane — how can I verify the azide formation step?
